signature: tests/fuzz/src/world.rs:4148 | FUZZ-ORACLE liveness (I-P#): after the wind-down's second claim pass market <key> still owes a lender # lamports (dust #) with lender_sol # (cap #)
finding: FUZZ-M10-24H-A (the final-tree 24 h run at 4f4849e, 2026-10-04, `run --profile all --duration 24h --jobs 4 --actions 400 --seed 20261004`, 6 of 52,272 runs, signature 561410b6; harness, not program): the wind-down's second claim pass (M10's fuzz follow-ups) required every lender owed at most CLAIM_DUST (1,000 lamports) and `lender_sol` at most the hooks' dust cap (0.01 SOL). This reproducer (minimised from 380 actions; cpmm seed 20265774) leaves the last lender, its shares all withdrawn (S = 0), owed 1,033 lamports with `real = claimed` and an empty pot, while `lender_sol` holds 1,913 lamports — `carry_r`, the realised accumulator's undistributed remainder: the entitlement (`acc`) and realised (`acc_r`) accumulators carry different remainders, up to S/WAD lamports each (S above 10^21 here, the share price near the rebase bound), so a lender's entitlement can exceed its realised allocation by thousands of lamports, and once the last shares leave that SOL is allocated to no lender (ECON §9.4 I-P6: the wind-down's residue is rounding plus rebase-orphan credits; the hooks' `invariants::lender::liveness` accepts an unpaid entitlement whose remainder is unallocated SOL within the cap). The full run also showed the two other shapes of the same oracle: a lender owed the carry while a later lender's touch moved its surplus to the pot only after the first one's claim (cpmm 20265774: 2,646 lamports owed, 3,298 in the pot), and `lender_sol` of 11.7–100 M lamports credited to one or two rebase-orphan shares after the lenders left during a vest (amm-v4 20285252, curve 20277239, cpmm 20285226, mixed 20295515; see fuzz-m10-24h-a-curve-orphan-credit.json). The program behaves as specified: the vest is released in full by the pass's crank (vest_bal 0 in every case), and the residue is ECON §9.5's rounding and rebase-orphan dust. Replay: `shortwin-fuzz replay tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz-m10-24h-a-cpmm-carry-owed.json`.

resolution: Resolved in the fuzzer, no program change: the second claim pass claims in two sequential rounds (as the hooks' wind-down), a lender may stay owed more than CLAIM_DUST only as rounding (no realised SOL of its own unclaimed, an empty pot, at most CLAIM_DUST plus the carries' bound — each share epoch's largest S over WAD, `World::carry_gap_bound` — plus the orphans' realised SOL, within the dust cap; `wind-down-owed-rounding`), and `lender_sol` may exceed the dust cap only by the realised SOL the rebase-orphan shares hold (`World::orphan_credit`: (S − Σ held)·acc_r now, each closed epoch after a rebase its orphans as measured while it was current times its acc_r_end; `wind-down-orphan-credit`). This file replays as a regression: the run must pass (`corpus_replays`, `wind_down_residue_on_fuzz_m10_24h_a`). Revised 2026-10-13 for AIR-07 (e1f873a): action 45's `trade` sells instead of buying (a 458876572 -> 458876573). Since AIR-07 the S1 settlement in action 40, which repays the last 731,882,875,130 borrowed tokens with T = 2 left (at most 1/1,000 of the claims), flushes the running 1,206,153,452-lamport vest to the epoch-0 shares as it rolls the epoch (before, the 10^9 rebase let it vest on in epoch 1), so every later credit leaves the accumulators other remainders: the original list left the last lender owed 943 lamports (1,101 just before AIR-07, 1,033 at 4f4849e), at most CLAIM_DUST, and no longer reached the carry-rounding branch this file pins. With the sell the last lender (no shares, real = claimed) is owed 2,149 lamports with an empty pot and lender_sol 2,332 (`wind-down-owed-rounding`), within the carries' bound (S peaks near 2.57e21: about 2,573 lamports).
